intent: Test the sensor-lead lever. Keep the iteration-7 design (mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, sensor span x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint) and move every sensor from y 0.05 to y 0.03 m. Target: s-bend and slalom progress back above 0.18, with max_error at or below 0.062 m, the oval finish rate at or above 65%, and oval steering_oscillation below 0.25.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) At mass 0.5 kg, the s-bend and slalom limit is sensor look-ahead rather than mass, so y 0.03 m raises their progress above 0.18. (2) The oval finish rate holds at or above 65% and oscillation stays below 0.25, since the oval has headroom at 0.208. (3) If s-bend progress falls below 0.14 or max_error rises above 0.065, the shorter lead is too late for the bends, so return to y 0.05 and test track 0.11 m next. Please report per-track progress, max_error and steering_oscillation, and the oval finish rate.
rationale: Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg, otherwise the iteration-6 design) is the best raced design at 315.27, up from 289.84. The gain came mostly from the oval, where the finish rate rose from 65% to 75% and steering_oscillation stayed at 0.208, under the 0.25 threshold. The mass lever did not help the other two tracks as hoped. S-bend progress fell from 0.181 to 0.140, and slalom progress stayed flat at 0.186 against 0.191. Both still end off_track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.064, at the 0.06 m floor, with zero or near-zero line loss. Mass is therefore not the limit on the s-bend and slalom. The Integrator's rule for 'progress stays at about 0.18 and 0.19 at mass 0.5 kg' applies, because the slalom is flat and the s-bend has moved backwards, so I move to the next lever: sensor lead. Every sensor y goes from 0.05 to 0.03 m. The x positions, the 0.016 m footprint, the 0.10 m track, the 0.10 m body, the 0.12 m width, the 0.03 m wheel radius and the 0.5 kg mass stay fixed, so the race isolates the lead change. Oval oscillation has headroom (0.208 against 0.25), so a shorter lead is affordable there. The lead reduction is also the step the Integrator named for the oscillation and drift cases. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress recover above about 0.18 with max_error no worse than 0.062, and the oval finish rate holds at 65% or more. Risk: a shorter look-ahead could raise max_error on the sharpest bends, which the s-bend race will show. If the s-bend or slalom gets worse, the next step is to return y to 0.05 and test wheel_track 0.11 or a sensor span change.
